canonical_statement: For a projective relative Q-factorial klt pair over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, the closed relative effective cone is the Minkowski sum of its log-canonical nonnegative part and countably many log-canonical-negative extremal rays generated by rational curves of bounded length; those rays are locally finite away from the nonnegative wall and each has its universal contraction.
domain_and_universes: universes u uK uN uC; algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k : Type uK; schemes X,S : Scheme.{u}; finite-dimensional real normed numerical-class space N1 : Type uN; rational-curve carrier : Type uC
conclusion: D.Conclusion: countable negative extremal rays with rational generators of anti-canonical degree at most twice the relative dimension; finite-support Minkowski decomposition; epsilon-local finiteness on the unit sphere; and a universal contraction for each ray.
representation_boundary: Pinned mathlib lacks definitions of klt pairs, Q-divisors, numerical curve classes, and extremal contractions. ConeTheoremData therefore types this vocabulary explicitly. Its Prop fields are input hypotheses only; none assumes a theorem conclusion. The field hypothesis is represented by k with Field, IsAlgClosed, and CharZero instances plus an explicit relation of the schemes to k.

killed: discarded decomposition, generators, local finiteness, and contractions

degenerate_cases: The index type may be empty; the finite-support list then reduces membership to the nonnegative part. Dimension zero makes the positive rational-curve length inequalities impossible, hence forces an empty ray family. Numerically trivial canonical pairing likewise permits no nonzero negative ray. Non-Q-factorial, non-klt, nonprojective, nonproper, non-normal, positive-characteristic, or non-algebraically-closed inputs are excluded by explicit binders or hypotheses.
status_boundary: This node elaborates the exact intake-selected target and distinguishes three structural mutations. It does not validate a source edition, credit the legacy scaffold, prove the cone theorem, or advance any dependent node.
